answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so voting weight reflects reachable, independently supported identities rather than raw node count. A sybil cluster with a sparse external cut has low conductance: only a limited fraction of walk probability crosses its boundary per step, mathematically bounding its aggregate influence absent outside attestations. A saffron-coded signal can flag such bottlenecks, while a finite horizon limits how far fabricated trust can spread.
